About

I’m a second-year secondary student at Al-Sayeda Zeinab Secondary School for Girls in Qena, and my main focus is robotics programming with Arduino. I also have a background in Java, HTML and CSS, and I’m still studying them. I started with robotics courses, and I now compete in national and international STEM events.

I like problems where technology meets people: a robot that reduces contact in an isolation ward, a startup idea tested in a bootcamp, a younger student who finally gets her first LED to blink. I also write poetry and play basketball, and both shape how I work in a team.

Featured project: Sanad (سند)

A mobile medical robot for patients with respiratory diseases in hospitals and isolation units. It moves on its own, avoids obstacles with ultrasonic sensors, and shows its status on OLED screens. The goal is less direct contact between staff and patients, and faster response, at low cost.

Arduino / ESP32Ultrasonic obstacle avoidanceOLED status displayTemperature · heart rate · SpO₂Database + appFire sensor alert

Sanad competed under the names MedSpark and Sanad and won across several competitions listed below.

Sanad supports the doctor and does not replace one. Any suggested treatment plan goes to the doctor for approval first.

Leadership and teaching

I help lead the Qena local event of the NASA International Space Apps Challenge, organise the team and give programming sessions. I also took part in the 2025 challenge and earned the Galactic Problem Solver certificate.

Chosen by the supervising engineer to help train younger students in robotics and programming, at the center and at governorate level. IVECOM’s CEO thanked me for supporting trainers and following up with trainees.
